angle: Behavioural design: the unit of reading, the trigger, the reward, the grace, the identity language, the return visit.
thesis: The path already wins day one and loses day two. Day 1 (Day1Landing.tsx) is a verse, three paragraphs and two questions — about three minutes. Day 2 (NewBelieverLessonCard.tsx) is a whole chapter plus a 285–464 word lesson plus two questions, with no closing moment beyond a grey line. The app's own promise on the path card reads "A 40-day journey. One short day at a time" (i18n path_new_promise) and it is kept once, then broken 39 times. The fix is already in the data: books/faith-pathway.json gives every day a named 3–7 verse reading (day 1: Ephesians 2:8-9) and both render paths throw it away, building the whole chapter from book+chapter (HomeScreen.tsx:855, NewBelieverLessonCard.tsx:94) while printing the small reference as the label. So this design makes days 2–40 the same size and the same shape as day 1, gives the returning person a door that says "coming back" out loud, replaces a fake streak with days actually read, points the daily nudge at their day instead of a global rotation, and puts one human next step at day 10. Nothing is stripped: the photo hero, the sage journey button, the paper reading surface, the questions and the whole chapter all stay — the chapter moves one tap down, it does not go away.
principles: One unit, every day, the same size. The day's named verses (3–7) are the unit; the whole chapter is one tap under it, never removed. Research P1: 'Day 1: 3–7 verses, plain language, one thought, already open'; cross-cutting 3: busyness is the #1 reason reading declines, the felt need is a smaller unit.

The trigger is their day, not a streak. The push says 'Day 7 of 40 is ready', sent at the hour they actually open. Research cross-cutting 6: one nudge a day, behaviour-inferred timing; guilt-framed streak reminders drive opt-out and uninstall.
The reward is the day closing, not a number going up. The same closing moment on day 1 and day 40, in the journey's own sage, with no second celebration stacked on it.

Grace is silent. The journey is day-numbered, not date-numbered (currentDay only advances on completion, coldStart.ts:169-191), so a missed day cannot leave anyone behind. Nothing in the UI ever mentions the gap.

Identity language counts what they actually did. Days read from pathwayProgress.completedDays, never the streak — recordStreakToday() fires on every HomeScreen mount (HomeScreen.tsx:786-795), so the streak counts app opens, and telling a new believer they have a '7-day streak' when they read three days is a lie the product tells on their behalf.
Never a graduation prompt, never a shame line, never an exclamation mark. (Comfort's 'Feeling Stronger?' is removed for good — the same instinct is banned here.)
Nothing here reaches production before Ashley sees it on a deploy preview and says so. The opening screen is owner-preview-gated, same class as the locked look.

journey.day0: Cold arrival at futuresdailyword.com (or the Sunday QR). App.tsx:68 silently stamps new_to_faith/source:'default' and enrolls the 40 days before React mounts — keep exactly. Day1Landing renders full-screen. New: one quiet line of two text chips under the eyebrow, 'I'm new to this' and 'I'm coming back'. Both open the same 40 days; the second changes the eyebrow and one sub-line, nothing else. Tapping either also sets dw_path_asked, because they have just answered the question Door 3 asks. Read stays the only button on the screen.
journey.first_session: Read expands in place: verse card, three pastoral paragraphs (with 'grace' carrying a dotted glossary term), Day 1's two Reflect & Respond questions, 'Mark as read'. markDay1Read stamps the day, advances to Day 2, records the streak, fires dw-reading-completed. Then at most two gates, never stacked, in the ruled order: PathAskedOnce (skipped now if they tapped an entry chip), then PushOptIn — with the hour picker pre-set to the hour they are reading right now instead of a hard 7am, and one added line: 'Day 2 lands tomorrow.' Then the tab shell. Total: about three minutes and two taps.
journey.return_visit: Home. Header (date, Daily Word, PathSwatch, LanguageSwitch), greeting that now names days read, then the journey hero: photo carousel, 'Day 6 of 40 · New & Returning to Faith', the day title, the progress bar, one sage button. Tap opens the full-screen Day N surface: day header, the day's 3–7 verses already open, the lesson, the two questions, 'Mark Complete', then 'Read the whole chapter' as a disclosure, then one quiet comfort line at the foot. Same three minutes as day 1.
journey.week2: Days 8–14 are identical in shape — that is the point. Two things arrive: at day 7 the closing card says 'Seven days. This is becoming yours' and the milestone banner (now counting days read, in the reader's language, no emoji, no exclamation) appears once; at day 10 the closing card carries one card — 'Someone at Futures would read this with you' — with a yes and a not-now, asked once, never again. Glossary terms run through day 14 in v1 and simply do not render on days 15–40.
journey.missed_day: Nothing happens. The journey does not advance, so Day 6 is still Day 6. On return the hero adds one line under the progress bar: 'Day 6 is where you left off.' No apology, no streak talk, no catch-up offer, no 'you missed two days'. The streak's one-freeze grace (streak.ts:65-75) keeps running underneath but is never shown on this path. Push resumes at their hour with the same neutral wording.
journey.seasonal: Out of scope for this persona in the first two weeks and deliberately not built here: the 40-day journey is already the reader's own time-boxed challenge, and layering a church-wide season on top of day 6 of 40 gives them two counters and two obligations. The seasonal read (research build item 6) belongs to congregation. The only seasonal touch on this path is the existing Sunday window, where the Sermon Notes row stays above the reading for QR guests — ruled, keep.

comfort_access: One quiet line at the foot of the Day N surface — "Going through something hard? Open comfort." — opens today's comfort chapter as a sub-view in comfortMode (Note + Close only) and returns to the journey on Close. It sets a session flag (dw_comfort_peek) and never writes dw_setup, so the saved path, the streak and the 40 days are untouched, and saveSetup's source!=='default' gate is never involved. It uses useSubView alone, no aria-modal, because the note drawer mounts above it (ruled after the 28-agent review). No graduation prompt, no count, no completion. Deliberately NOT placed on the I'm-New home: Ashley ruled that every line on that screen relates to the sage journey button, and the PathSwatch already reaches "I'm going through something hard" from the header in two taps. Whether the line also belongs at the foot of Home is his call, not mine (see open decisions). Research: persona 6, "a persistent one-tap 'I need comfort now' that opens comfort without switching the saved path — crisis is not a persona someone chooses on a good day." The crisis-keyword safety flow and region-correct lines are a cross-path build owned by the comfort design, not this one; this path only needs the door.
reminders: One a day, never more. Content is their day, not a global rotation: "Day 7 of 40 is ready. About three minutes." Timing starts behaviour-informed on day one — the PushOptIn hour select is pre-set to the hour they are reading at that moment instead of a hard 7am — and becomes behaviour-inferred once there are five completions, taking the median local hour from dw_read_hours, but only where the person never set an hour themselves (dw_push_hour_source stays 'user' the moment they touch the picker in PushOptIn or MoreScreen). Suppressed entirely on a day already completed, using the same once-per-local-day ledger and local en-CA date axis as everything else. Never mentions a streak, a loss, a gap or a missed day, and never carries an exclamation mark. Where push is unsupported — including every deploy preview and the futures.church proxy, since pushSupported() allowlists only futuresdailyword.com, www and localhost — the existing calendar fallback stands unchanged, which also means this can only be verified on prod or localhost, never on the preview Ashley reviews. Research: cross-cutting 6 (one nudge a day, timed to when the person actually opens, Duolingo's behaviour-inferred timing; guilt framing drives opt-out and uninstall) and persona 2's reminder journey.
instrumentation: dw_device_id — a random id written on first open behind the existing dw_cookie_consent gate and misc-synced, so track() can report a person who has no email yet. Today track() only writes to Supabase when dw_profile.email exists (analytics.ts:69-81), which means every brand-new believer on day 1 is invisible server-side and only GA4 sees them. This is the single blocking gap: the persona whose retention we most need to measure is the one we cannot currently count.
journey_entry_chosen — detail 'new' | 'returning'. Proves whether the returning door is used at all, and lets every metric below split by entry. Research P1's headline test.
journey_day_open — detail: day number. Session starts, by day.
journey_day_complete — detail: day number. The completion curve, and the number that answers the day-2 cliff.

journey_chapter_open — detail: day number. The guard on the smaller unit: if this runs high, readers wanted the chapter and the disclosure is doing its job; if it runs near zero and completion is up, the small unit was right.
journey_term_open — detail: the term. Glossary tap rate, research P1's third test.
journey_question_answered — detail: day:index. Whether Reflect & Respond is used or scrolled past.
journey_return — detail: days since last completion. Feeds D1/D7/D14 and tells us whether the left-off line lands on people who came back after a gap.
journey_connect_request — detail: campus. Day-10 relational move, accept rate.
push_opt_out — currently unmeasured. Research cross-cutting 6 makes this the canary on reminder wording.

Rollup: D1 / D7 / D14 by path and by entry, day-2 completion rate as a share of day-1 completions, median seconds day 1 vs day 2 (before and after the unit change), chapter-open rate, glossary tap rate, push opt-out rate, connect-request rate at day 10. Research build item 1: 'Instrumentation. D1/D7/D30 by path... Nothing above can be tested without it, and no public source will ever supply it.'
Every one of these names must be added to TRACKED_EVENTS (analytics.ts:24-31) or track() silently drops it — the allow-list is a hardcoded array and is the usual reason a new event never appears.
self_serve_levers: Campus welcome item — the day-10 invitation copy and the name of who reaches out come from campus_content where type='welcome', published by the campus pastor at /staff through an intake_questions row (config.publish='campus_corner', config.itemType='welcome'). One-time developer cost: add "welcome" to CORNER_TYPES (netlify/functions/lib/intake-core.js:40) and insert one intake_questions row. After that the pastor edits it, adds it, removes it and re-words it themselves, forever, with no deploy. If no campus item exists, the card falls back to the default copy above.

The forty days themselves — books/faith-pathway.json is one file: lesson text, day titles, themes, the two questions per day in four languages, the reading reference and (new) the glossary terms. Editing it needs no code and no component change; /books/* is already network-first with cache as offline fallback (PR #84), so returning readers see the edit on the second open after deploy. This is Ashley's lever, not a campus pastor's — the teaching is his voice.

The reading unit per day — because the verse range now comes from reading.verses in that same JSON, shortening or lengthening any day is a content edit, not a code change. Set verses to the whole chapter's range on a day that deserves it and that day serves the whole chapter.
Sunday QR window — the Sermon Notes row above the reading for guests, already campus-owned through the existing intake and the sermon publish flow. Unchanged.
Reminder hour and push on/off — the reader's own lever in MoreScreen; the inferred hour never overrides a hand-set one.
Language — LanguageSwitch on the Day 1 landing and in the Home header; four languages already carried through every string this design adds.
Path — the PathSwatch pill on Home, the landing line, the asked-once link and Settings, all four doors into the one ChoosePathSheet. Untouched.

Not self-serve, and honestly so: push templates and the milestone list stay hardcoded in push-send.js and streak.ts. A campus pastor should not be editing notification copy that goes to every congregation, and pretending otherwise would mean building an admin surface nobody asked for.

open_decisions: Approve the two entry chips on the Superdesign-locked Day 1 landing. This is a change to the opening screen — the same class as the rebuild you reverted on 1 Sep — so it ships behind a deploy preview and merges only on your word. If the answer is no, everything else in this design still stands; the returning person simply keeps the single 'Read' door.

Reorder days 2–7 toward Gospel narrative before doctrine? The research says front-loading accessible passages raised plan completion, and days 1–14 are currently almost all epistles. This is your teaching sequence and your call. Not built.
Who receives the day-10 connect request at each campus, and does it go to the campus pastor or to one hub inbox? The plumbing works either way; the choice is pastoral.
Approve the glossary terms for days 1–14 in English before they are translated. Claude drafts, you approve — the standing rule for translated content, and these sit inside your lesson text.

Does the comfort line also belong at the foot of the I'm-New home, or only inside the Day N reading? Your 1 Sep ruling says every line on that home relates to the sage button; a comfort line does not. I have kept it off Home. Duty of care argues the other way.
Keep the 'Show me now' next-day peek? It is one tap per day, but a determined reader can still walk all forty days in an evening and lose the forty-day shape. Currently kept.
Does 'days read' replace the streak on this path everywhere — including anywhere else the streak number surfaces for a new believer — or only in the greeting and the milestone banner?
risks: The smaller unit could mean less scripture read overall. Mitigated by keeping the whole chapter one tap away and by measuring journey_chapter_open — if that rate is high and completion is flat, the unit was not the problem and the change should be reverted.

Changing the Day 1 landing is the exact class of change that was reverted on 1 Sep. Preview link, Ashley's explicit approval, no merge without his word. The chips are two text links, not a restructure, and Read stays the only button.

GreetingSection is shared by all five personas. The milestone rewrite must be pinned by tests for congregation, deeper_study and pastor_leader so a fix aimed at one path does not silently change four.
push_subscriptions needs two columns. Migration goes in the repo — a stale out-of-repo migration is what once deleted a live database three days before a flight.

Any write to dw_pathway_progress must merge into what is currently in localStorage and touch only its own fields. Rebuilding it from React state destroyed nine days of a real user's progress in PR #64. The closing card reads it; it must not rewrite it.
dw_device_id is a new identifier. It must sit behind the existing dw_cookie_consent gate, must never be joined to a person before they give an email, and must never appear in a URL.

Editing books/faith-pathway.json is invisible to returning devices unless /books/* is still network-first. It is (PR #84) — confirm before shipping content, and no sw.js change means no CACHE_NAME / SW_VERSION bump is needed. If sw.js is touched for any reason, bump CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION together.

Push cannot be verified on the deploy preview or the futures.church proxy — pushSupported() allowlists only futuresdailyword.com, www and localhost. Verify the day-aware payload on prod or localhost, never on the preview.
The glossary content is 14 days across four languages. If it slips, ship everything else — the renderer degrades to plain text when terms is absent, so no day breaks.
The day-10 invitation asks a new believer for contact with a stranger. One ask, one dismissal, never repeated, and 'Not now' must be as prominent as 'Yes'.
Day1Landing.test.tsx counts CTAs by regex and will fail on the two chips. That failure is the test doing its job — update it deliberately, do not loosen the pattern.
